claims.claim: Amazon SQS standard queues use at-least-once delivery and best-effort ordering.
claims.summary: The official queue-types guide defines at-least-once delivery and best-effort ordering for standard queues.

claims.claim: FIFO queues preserve message order and support exactly-once processing.
claims.summary: The official FIFO queues guide identifies FIFO delivery and exactly-once processing as its central features.

claims.claim: Receiving a message makes it temporarily invisible to other consumers.
claims.summary: The official visibility-timeout guide states that a received message remains in the queue but becomes temporarily invisible to other consumers.

claims.claim: If a consumer does not delete a received message before its visibility timeout expires, SQS can make it visible for another processing attempt.
claims.summary: The official visibility-timeout guide explains that an undeleted message becomes visible again and can be retrieved for another processing attempt.

claims.claim: Configure a dead-letter queue with a redrive policy to isolate messages that are not processed successfully.
claims.summary: The official dead-letter queue guide explains that source queues target DLQs for unsuccessfully processed messages and that redrive policies specify the receive threshold.

claims.claim: Long polling reduces empty `ReceiveMessage` responses and can reduce cost.
claims.summary: The official long-polling guide recommends it to decrease empty receives and reduce SQS cost.
